definitions.explanation: A state of extreme poverty or want, where one lacks the basic necessities of life. A formal, literary word used in written Japanese and historical descriptions.

examples.japanese: {戦後|せんご}は{窮乏|きゅうぼう}した{生活|せいかつ}が{続|つづ}いた。
examples.english: After the war, a life of destitution continued.

examples.japanese: {長引|ながび}く{不況|ふきょう}で{国民|こくみん}の{窮乏|きゅうぼう}が{深|ふか}まった。
examples.english: The prolonged recession deepened the poverty of the people.

examples.japanese: {窮乏|きゅうぼう}の{中|なか}でも{人々|ひとびと}は{助|たす}け{合|あ}い、{困難|こんなん}を{乗|の}り{越|こ}えた。
examples.english: Even in the midst of destitution, people helped one another and overcame hardship.

notes:
USAGE:
A formal noun that also functions as a する verb: {窮乏|きゅうぼう}する (to become destitute). Often used in historical writing about wartime or post-war Japan, and in descriptions of economic hardship.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {窮乏|きゅうぼう}した{生活|せいかつ} (a destitute life)
- {窮乏|きゅうぼう}に{耐|た}える (to endure poverty)
- {窮乏|きゅうぼう}が{深|ふか}まる (poverty deepens)
- {窮乏|きゅうぼう}から{抜|ぬ}け{出|だ}す (to escape from poverty)

SIMILAR WORDS:
{貧困|ひんこん} (poverty) is the most common neutral term. {窮乏|きゅうぼう} emphasizes severe, pressing want and is more literary.
